Elias Schlegel, a member of this family, was a distinguished dramatic writer in his own time; and some of his plays are, I believe, acted in Germany at the present day.

arxiv-1705-09601.title: Introduction to Particle Accelerators and their Limitations
arxiv-1705-09601.creator: B.J. Holzer
arxiv-1705-09601.description: Abstract The paper gives an overview of the principles of particle accelerators and their historical development. After introducing the basic concepts, the main emphasis is on sketching the layout of modern storage rings and discussing their limitations in terms of energy and machine performance.

arxiv-2012-08653.title: Optimization of Quantum-dot Qubit Fabrication via Machine Learning
arxiv-2012-08653.creator: Antonio B. Mei, Ivan Milosavljevic, Amanda L. Simpson, Valerie A. Smetanka, Colin P. Feeney, Shay M. Seguin, Sieu D. Ha, Wonill Ha, Matthew D. Reed

Ha, Wonill Ha, Matthew D. Reed. Precise nanofabrication represents a critical challenge to developing semiconductor quantum-dot qubits for practical quantum computation. Here, we design and train a convolutional neural network to interpret in-line scanning electron micrographs and quantify qualitative features affecting device functionality.

arxiv-2012-10986.title: Biased Models Have Biased Explanations
arxiv-2012-10986.creator: Aditya Jain, Manish Reddy, Joydeep Ghosh
arxiv-2012-10986.description: Abstract We study fairness in Machine Learning (FairML) through the lens of attribute-based explanations generated for machine learning models. Our hypothesis is: Biased Models have Biased Explanations . To establish that, we first translate existing statistical notions of group fairness and define these notions in terms of explanations given by the model.

arxiv-2103-01415.title: A Survey of Deep Learning Techniques for Weed Detection from Images
arxiv-2103-01415.creator: A S M Mahmudul Hasan, Ferdous Sohel, Dean Diepeveen, Hamid Laga, Michael G.K. Jones
arxiv-2103-01415.description: Abstract The rapid advances in Deep Learning (DL) techniques have enabled rapid detection, localisation, and recognition of objects from images or videos. DL techniques are now being used in many applications related to agriculture and farming. Automatic detection and classification of weeds can play an important role in weed management and so contribute to higher yields.

arxiv-2105-13003.title: Rethinking InfoNCE: How Many Negative Samples Do You Need?
arxiv-2105-13003.creator: Chuhan Wu Fangzhao Wu Yongfeng Huang
arxiv-2105-13003.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chuhan Wu Fangzhao Wu Yongfeng Huang. InfoNCE loss is a widely used loss function for contrastive model training. It aims to estimate the mutual information between a pair of variables by discriminating between each positive pair and its associated K K negative pairs. It is proved that when the sample labels are clean, the lower bound of mutual information estimation is tighter when more negative samples are incorporated, which usually yields better model performance.

arxiv-2109-08164.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jorick S. Vink, 1. Massive stars have strong stellar winds that direct their evolution through the upper Hertzsprung-Russell diagram and determine the black hole mass function. Secondly, wind strength dictates the atmospheric structure that sets the ionising flux. Thirdly, the wind directly intervenes with the stellar envelope structure, which is decisive for both single star and binary evolution, affecting predictions for gravitational wave events.

arxiv-2308-14737.title: Flexible Techniques for Differentiable Rendering with 3D Gaussians
arxiv-2308-14737.creator: Leonid Keselman, Martial Hebert
arxiv-2308-14737.description: Abstract Fast, reliable shape reconstruction is an essential ingredient in many computer vision applications. Neural Radiance Fields demonstrated that photorealistic novel view synthesis is within reach, but was gated by performance requirements for fast reconstruction of real scenes and objects. Several recent approaches have built on alternative shape representations, in particular, 3D Gaussians.

arxiv-2310-01570.title: Magnetization of Antiferromagnetic Cactus Graph Model with Exact Dimer Ground State
arxiv-2310-01570.creator: Pratyay Ghosh
arxiv-2310-01570.description: Abstract We introduce and explore the magnetization behavior in a quantum spin system on a cactus graph, deemed the Cactus Graph Model (CGM), featuring an exact dimer singlet ground state. We analyze the singlet-triplet gap, interactions among excited triplets, and correlated hopping under an external magnetic field using a strong coupling expansion.

arxiv-2410-10508.title: Everyday Speech in the Indian Subcontinent
arxiv-2410-10508.creator: Utkarsh Pathak, Chandra sai krishna G, Sujitha Sathiyamoorthy, Keshav Agarwal, Hema A Murthy
arxiv-2410-10508.description: Abstract India has 1369 languages of which 22 are official. About 13 different scripts are used to represent these languages. A Common Label Set(CLS) was developed based on phonetics to address the issue of large vocabulary of units required in the End-to-End(E2E) framework for multilingual synthesis. The Indian language text is first converted to CLS.

arxiv-2411-10167.title: Gamma Distribution for Equilibrium Analysis of Discrete Stochastic Logistic Population Models
arxiv-2411-10167.creator: Haiyan Wang
arxiv-2411-10167.description: Abstract Stochastic models play an essential role in accounting for the variability and unpredictability seen in real-world. This paper focuses on the application of the gamma distribution to analysis of the stationary distributions of populations governed by the discrete stochastic logistic equation at equilibrium.

arxiv-2505-07356.title: Inverse Bauschinger Effect in Active Ultrastable Glasses
arxiv-2505-07356.creator: Rashmi Priya 1, Smarajit Karmakar 1
arxiv-2505-07356.description: Abstract Memory effects in amorphous materials have been widely studied because of their possible widespread future applications. We show here that ultrastable glasses can exhibit a transient reversible memory effect when subjected to both a local driving force via Run-and-tumble active particles and global shear.

arxiv-2601-11774.title: A wafer-scale ultrasensitive programmable chiroptical sensor
arxiv-2601-11774.creator: Haoyu Xie, Jichao Fan, Zarif Ahmad Razin Bhuiyan, Saqlain Raza, Mohammad Mohammadi, Cheng Guo, Yunshan Wang, Jun Liu, Weilu Gao
arxiv-2601-11774.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Haoyu Xie, Jichao Fan, Zarif Ahmad Razin Bhuiyan, Saqlain Raza, Mohammad Mohammadi, Cheng Guo, Yunshan Wang, Jun Liu, Weilu Gao. Chiroptical enantioselective sensing is gaining traction across various applications. However, intrinsic molecular chiroptical responses are weak, and existing amplification approaches add synthesis, manufacturing, or operational complexity that limits sensitivity, scalability, and dynamic control. Here, we present a fundamentally new sensing paradigm merging adsorption-driven chirality induction with wafer-scale optical transduction in a programmable heterostructure containing twisted aligned carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and phase change materials (PCMs).

pmc-11506335.title: A TRilogy of ATR’s Non-Canonical Roles Throughout the Cell Cycle and Its Relation to Cancer
pmc-11506335.creator: Yoon Ki Joo, Carlos Ramirez, Lilian Kabeche
pmc-11506335.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryIn this review, we introduce and summarize the canonical roles of Ataxia Telangiectasia and Rad3-related protein (ATR) in the DNA damage response (DDR) pathway. More importantly, we also summarize the most recent discoveries of ATR’s non-canonical roles in regulating nuclear membrane integrity, mechanical force, chromosome segregation, and its role in PML bodies and discuss how they are relevant to the current progress of ATR inhibitors in clinical trials.

pmc-12650495.creator: Thiago Prudente Bartholo, Luis Cristóvão Porto, Roberto Pozzan, Adriana Nascimento, Barbara Beatriz Garcia Raskovisch Bartholo, Rogerio Rufino, Cláudia Henrique da Costa
pmc-12650495.description: Background: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a complex condition influenced by both environmental and genetic factors. Among the genetic determinants, polymorphisms in the CHRNA3/5 and EPHX1 genes have been implicated in nicotine dependence and susceptibility to COPD in several populations. However, evidence remains limited in admixed populations such as Brazilians.

pmc-12915350.title: Evaluating the Influence of Health Education Programs on Quality of Life in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Saudi Arabia
pmc-12915350.creator: Raneem Salem, Ayesha Nuzhat, Ghadeer Hassonah, Fatimah Al Barqi, Asirvatham Alwin Robert
pmc-12915350.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and ObjectiveThe prevalence of type 2 diabetes in Saudi Arabia is steadily rising, resulting in multiple complications that negatively influence patients’ quality of life (QOL) and further add to the worldwide burden of chronic diseases. This study aimed to evaluate the QOL of individuals with diabetes and to determine the effect of structured health education programs on improving their QOL.MethodsA quasi-experimental study was carried out after obtaining ethical approval.

pmc-13227683.creator: Ju-Ying Chien, Li-Lian Chao, Chien-Ming Shih, Chia-Hui Shen, Sung-Yuan Hu
pmc-13227683.description: BackgroundIntestinal parasitic infections remain among the most common infectious diseases worldwide, posing significant public health challenges. Blastocystis spp., in particular, has emerged as the most prevalent microorganism detected in human stool examinations in recent years. Accumulating evidence suggests a potential association between specific Blastocystis subtypes and gastrointestinal disturbances.
